newsitem.title: USA: Greenwich Air to build plant in Senegal.
newsitem.headline: Greenwich Air to build plant in Senegal.

text.p: Greenwich Air Services Inc Tuesday said its Greenwich Turbine Inc subsidiary has agreed with a Senegalese electric utility firm to build in Dakar a 50-megawatt gas turbine power station, valued at $50 million.
Greenwich, which will own and operate the facility for 15 years, estimates the plant will produce $300 million in electric utility revenues over that period.
The 18-month project is expected to begin in the summer of 1997.

The firm also said it shipped the first of two 25-megawatt gas turbine power stations to Egypt, and signed a letter of intent with USX-Marathon Group's Marathon Oil to operate and maintain six gas turbine power plants in Ecuador.
Greenwich said the shipment of remanufactured gas turbine electrical power plants was to Cairo-based First Power.

Under the terms of a previously signed contract, valued at $20 million over a five-year period, Greenwich will supply and install the equipment and provide on-going management services including the operation and maintenance of the power plant over the life of the agreement.
The gas turbine electric power plants in Ecuador are valued at more than $1 million annually, the company said
